samples.prompt: user: My Node service crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined at startup. Where should I look first?
samples.response:
Root cause: Accessing a property on an undefined variable at startup.
Patch: Immediately check the first lines of your main entry file (e.g., index.js or app.js) for any object property access without prior existence checks.
Next check: Add console logs or breakpoints before the failing line to verify variable initialization. Confirm environment variables or config files are loaded correctly before use.

samples.prompt: user: My Node service crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined at startup. Where should I look first?
samples.response: Start by identifying which variable is undefined at startup. Check the stack trace to find the exact file and line number causing the error. Then, review the code at that location to see which object or variable is being accessed. Common causes include missing environment variables, uninitialized configuration objects, or asynchronous data not yet loaded. Verify that all required dependencies and configurations are properly set before the code runs. Adding console.log statements before the error line can help trace the undefined value. Also, ensure that any asynchronous initialization completes before accessing its results.

Time Allocation: Divide your available hours into focused work blocks (e.g., 90 minutes) with short breaks (10-15 minutes) to maintain energy. 3. Eliminate Distractions: Turn off notifications, close unrelated tabs/apps, and inform others you need uninterrupted time. 4. Quick Wins First: Start with tasks that can be completed quickly to build momentum. 5. Delegate if Possible: Identify any tasks that can be handed off to teammates. 6. Regular Check-ins: Set checkpoints every 2-3 hours to assess progress and adjust priorities. 7. Prepare for Submission: Reserve the last hour for final testing, review, and packaging. Stay focused and keep hydrated. You can do this!
